key_insight: 2D/3D perovskite band alignment is highly sensitive to surface termination, composition, and interface-induced polarization, so small chemical changes can shift device energetics by hundreds of meV.
engineering_relevance: These results guide interface engineering for more stable, passivated perovskite solar cells by showing which 2D/3D combinations are most likely to improve energy alignment and reduce degradation.
method: Consistent calculation of work function, electron affinity, and band offsets
evidence_signal: The abstract reports preliminary computed band offset ranges of about 0.2–0.7 eV for valence bands and roughly 0.25 eV for conduction bands, with work functions strongly dependent on surface cleavage and chemistry.
watch_item: The results are preliminary and appear to depend strongly on idealized surface/interface models, so experimental validation and disorder effects may change the predicted offsets.
paper_title: Material chemical composition impacts on the band alignments: preliminary results on the 3D/2D perovskite interfaces
